title: Local scalar Dolbeault lemma on complex Euclidean space
statement: Use the usual real and complex fields $\mathbf R$ and $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq0$, let $U\subset\mathbf C^n$ be open, and let $a\in U$. A smooth scalar $(0,q)$-form on $U$ means a finite sum $\alpha=\sum_{|J|=q}f_J\,d\bar z_J$ with $f_J:U\to\mathbf C$ smooth, where $J$ ranges over increasing subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $d\bar z_J$ is the corresponding wedge; for $q>n$ this space is zero. Define $\bar\partial\alpha=\sum_{j,J}(\partial f_J/\partial\bar z_j)\,d\bar z_j\wedge d\bar z_J$, where $\partial/\partial\bar z_j=\tfrac12(\partial/\partial x_j+i\partial/\partial y_j)$ and $z_j=x_j+iy_j$. For $q\geq1$, every such $\alpha$ with $\bar\partial\alpha=0$ admits an open neighborhood $V\subset U$ of $a$ and a smooth scalar $(0,q-1)$-form $\beta$ on $V$ with $\bar\partial\beta=\alpha|_V$. For $q=0$, a smooth function $f$ on $U$ satisfies $\bar\partial f=0$ if and only if $f$ is holomorphic on $U$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. I §3.C, formula (3.14) and Cauchy--Riemann criterion, printed pp.23--24; I §3.E, Lemma (3.29), smooth scalar case p=0, printed pp.28--29. The point a is translated to 0; only local solvability, not solvability on all of U, is asserted.

proof.text: First record $\bar\partial^2=0$ on these local forms. Apply [lem-sfb-chart-exterior-derivative-square-zero] to each point of a chart in $\mathbf R^{2n}$ with complex-valued forms (extend a coefficient arbitrarily outside the chart; smoothness at the chosen interior point is unchanged). Substitute $dx_j=(dz_j+d\bar z_j)/2$ and $dy_j=(dz_j-d\bar z_j)/(2i)$ in exterior differentiation. The component that increases antiholomorphic degree by two in $d^2$ is exactly $\bar\partial^2$; independence of the wedge basis makes that component zero. This uses the real exterior derivative of the cited node, not a previously assumed exactness theorem.

source.place: I §3.C, formulas (3.14)--(3.17), printed p.24; I §1.A exterior differentiation; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: For degree zero fix $x\in U$ and let $A=D_{\mathbf R}f(x)$, which exists by smoothness. With $e_j$ the complex coordinate basis, the equation $f_{\bar z_j}=0$ is $A(e_j)+iA(ie_j)=0$, equivalently $A(ie_j)=iA(e_j)$. Expanding a vector as $\sum_j(x_j e_j+y_j ie_j)$ shows that these equations are equivalent to $A(iv)=iA(v)$ for every $v$. A real-linear map with this property is complex-linear, since $A((s+it)v)=sA(v)+tA(iv)$; its continuity is already part of being a real Fréchet derivative. Apply [lem-sfb-real-derivative-complex-linear], locally extending $f$ off $U$ if needed, to conclude that $f$ is complex differentiable at $x$ exactly when all these equations hold. Doing this at every $x$ gives precisely holomorphicity on $U$.

source.place: I §3.C, formula (3.14) and Cauchy--Riemann criterion, printed p.24; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: If $q>n$, the form is zero and $\beta=0$ on $U$ suffices; this also handles every $q\geq1$ when $n=0$. Suppose $1\leq q\leq n$. Choose radii $0<r_j<R_j$ so that the polydisc $P^n=\prod_jD(a_j,R_j)$ lies in $U$. Put $P^k=\prod_{j\leq k}D(a_j,R_j)\times\prod_{j>k}D(a_j,r_j)$. We will descend from a closed form $\gamma_n=\alpha|_{P^n}$ to closed forms $\gamma_k$ on $P^k$ whose wedge monomials use only $d\bar z_1,\ldots,d\bar z_k$, subtracting an explicit $\bar\partial$ at each stage. The initial invariant holds because there are only $n$ coordinates.

source.place: I §8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61; I §3.E, Lemma (3.29), localization at a point; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: At stage $k\geq1$ write $\gamma_k=d\bar z_k\wedge f+g$, where $f$ and $g$ use only wedge indices less than $k$, of degrees $q-1$ and $q$ respectively. For every $j>k$, the coefficient of $d\bar z_j\wedge d\bar z_J$ in $\bar\partial\gamma_k$ is, up to the ordering sign, $\partial(\gamma_k)_J/\partial\bar z_j$: no other derivative can give this monomial, since $\gamma_k$ has no index greater than $k$. Closedness therefore says that all coefficients of $f$ and $g$ are killed by $\partial/\partial\bar z_j$ for $j>k$. This conclusion uses coefficient independence, not a holomorphic-parameter assertion left implicit.

source.place: I §8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61, decomposition by the highest occurring differential; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-cauchy-transform-parameters] in variable $z_k$, with all other coordinates as real parameters, and radii $r_k<R_k$. For each coefficient $f_J$ let $b_J=T_{\chi_k}f_J$ and put $b_k=\sum_J b_Jd\bar z_J$ on $P^{k-1}$. The cited node gives joint smoothness and $\partial b_J/\partial\bar z_k=f_J$. For $j>k$, its real parameter derivative identities and complex-linearity give $\partial b_J/\partial\bar z_j=T_{\chi_k}(\partial f_J/\partial\bar z_j)=0$, by step 4. Consequently the coordinate formula is $\bar\partial b_k=d\bar z_k\wedge f+\sum_{j<k,J}(\partial b_J/\partial\bar z_j)d\bar z_j\wedge d\bar z_J$. The parameter domain is the product of the remaining discs in $P^k$, an open subset of $\mathbf R^{2n-2}$; no compact support of $f_J$ in those parameters is assumed.

source.place: I §8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61, cutoff partial convolution; I §3.A, Corollary (3.4), printed p.21; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Define $\gamma_{k-1}=\gamma_k|_{P^{k-1}}-\bar\partial b_k$. The displayed formula in step 5 cancels exactly its $d\bar z_k$ terms and introduces no index greater than $k$, so only indices less than $k$ remain. It is closed because $\bar\partial\gamma_k=0$ and $\bar\partial^2b_k=0$ by step 1. This proves the descent invariant and permits the next stage. After the finite stages $k=n,\ldots,1$, the positive-degree form $\gamma_0$ has no available wedge indices and is zero. Restrict every $b_k$ to $V=P^0$ and set $\beta=\sum_{k=1}^n b_k|_V$. Telescoping the defining equalities gives $\bar\partial\beta=\alpha|_V$. The set $V$ is an open neighborhood of $a$ inside $U$, and all restrictions and this finite sum preserve smoothness.

lean.statement: theorem local_scalar_dolbeault (n q : ℕ) (U : Set (Fin n → ℂ)) (hU : IsOpen U) (a : Fin n → ℂ) (ha : a ∈ U) (α : ScalarAntiholomorphicForm n (q + 1) U) (hα : IsSmoothScalarForm α) (hclosed : scalarDolbeault α = 0) : ∃ (V : Set (Fin n → ℂ)) (_hV : IsOpen V) (hVU : V ⊆ U), a ∈ V ∧ ∃ β : ScalarAntiholomorphicForm n q V, IsSmoothScalarForm β ∧ scalarDolbeault β = restrictScalarForm hVU α
